info.name: ClaimAssist Complete Collection
info.description: Production-quality Postman collection for ClaimAssist insurance AI microservices platform. Comprehensive testing and debugging tool covering all REST endpoints, authentication, AI/LLM flows, Kafka event-driven architecture, Redis caching, and end-to-end business flows.

request.description: Check API Gateway health status including liveness and readiness probes
Check Customer Service health status
Check Claims Service health status including Kafka connectivity
Check Agent Service health status including Ollama, Kafka, and Redis connectivity
Get Gateway build and application information
Get available metrics endpoints for Gateway
Get Prometheus-formatted metrics for monitoring and observability
Create a new customer account with valid credentials
Attempt to signup with duplicate email - should fail
Attempt signup with invalid email format
Attempt signup with weak password (< 8 characters)
Attempt signup missing required fields
Initiate OAuth2 PKCE authorization flow with Keycloak. Returns redirect to Keycloak login page.
Handle OAuth2 callback from Keycloak with authorization code. Exchanges code for tokens.
Handle OAuth2 error callback when user denies authorization
Handle callback missing authorization code
Refresh access token using valid refresh token
Attempt token refresh with invalid refresh token
Logout user and invalidate refresh token
Update authenticated customer's profile information
Delete authenticated customer's account
Create a new insurance policy for the authenticated customer
Retrieve all policies for the authenticated customer (uses cached query service)
Retrieve a specific policy by ID for the authenticated customer
Update an existing policy for the authenticated customer
Delete a policy for the authenticated customer
Submit a new insurance claim with idempotency key to prevent duplicates
Retrieve all claims for the authenticated customer
Retrieve a specific claim by ID
Update claim status (requires UPDATE_STATUS permission). Triggers state machine validation.
Stream AI agent response using Server-Sent Events. Agent will use tools to retrieve claim status, policy coverage, and documents before responding.
Retrieve complete conversation history for a claim including all user messages and AI responses with tool calls
Agent will invoke get_claim_status tool to retrieve current claim status and history
Agent will invoke get_policy_coverage tool to retrieve policy details including deductible and coverage limits
Agent will invoke get_claim_documents tool to retrieve submitted documents with OCR status and fraud scores
Agent will invoke propose_claim_update tool to request status change. This triggers Kafka saga to claims-service for validation and application.
Test agent behavior with empty message - should trigger validation error
Test agent behavior with non-existent claim ID - tools should return NOT_FOUND errors
Test agent behavior with invalid authentication token
Internal API to get policy coverage. Used by agent-service. Supports both USER tokens and SERVICE tokens with X-User-Id header.
Internal API to get claim status with full history. Used by agent-service.
Internal API to get claim documents with OCR status and fraud scores. Used by agent-service.
Internal API to check if user has specific permission on a claim. Used by agent-service for tool authorization.
Test gateway routing to customer-service via /customer/** path
Test gateway routing to claims-service via /claims/** path
Test gateway routing to agent-service via /agent/** path
Test gateway routing to customer-service via /policies/** path
Test gateway behavior with invalid route - should return 404
Step 1: Create new customer account
Step 2: Create insurance policy for the customer
Step 3: Submit an insurance claim against the policy
Step 4: Use AI agent to inquire about claim status and coverage (triggers tool calls)
Step 5: Verify final claim status after AI interaction
Step 1: Agent proposes status change via propose_claim_update tool
Step 2: Verify agent recorded the proposal in conversation history (saga initiated)
Step 3: Verify claim status was updated by Kafka saga (after claims-service processes the event)
Public route - should work without authentication token
Public health endpoint - should work without authentication
Protected route - should fail with 401 without token
Protected route - should fail with 401 with invalid token
Protected route - should succeed with valid token
Attempt to access another customer's policy - should fail with 404 (security through obscurity)
Attempt to update another customer's claim - should fail with 404 or 403
Missing coveragePlanId - should fail validation
Incident date in future - should fail validation
Missing policyId - should fail validation
Request non-existent policy - should return 404
Request non-existent claim - should return 404
Request conversation for non-existent claim - should return empty array or 404
Attempt invalid status transition - should fail state machine validation
Attempt to submit claim for policy you don't own - should fail authorization
First request should hit database (cache miss) - observe response time
Second request should hit Redis cache (cache hit) - observe faster response time
Agent first reads claim status - caches result in Redis
Agent proposes update - should invalidate claim status cache
Agent reads claim status again - should fetch fresh data from backend (cache was invalidated)
